_説明: Explanations shown when you click a word in the code (English). tools/make_glossaries.py makes this file from the dictionaries in tools/glossary/en/ (fix the dictionaries, not this file).
datasets: Practice datasets (iris, breast cancer, handwritten digits and so on)
load_iris: The iris data (150 flowers, 4 features, 3 species)
load_breast_cancer: Breast cancer diagnosis data (569 cases, 30 features, benign or malignant)
return_X_y: True returns only the features (X) and the answers (y)
make_blobs: Makes practice data of points in clumps
make_moons: Makes practice data shaped like two interlocking crescents
n_samples: The number of data points to make
centers: The number of clumps (or their centers)
cluster_std: The spread of the clumps (standard deviation)
model_selection: Splitting data, cross-validation, grid search and so on
train_test_split: Splits data into training and test sets
train_test_split.random_state: Fixes the random numbers for the split (same result every time)
train_test_split.stratify: Splits so the answers' proportions are the same in training and test
random_state: A number that fixes the random numbers. The same number gives the same result every time
cross_val_score.cv: How many parts to split into for cross-validation (or how to split)
cross_val_score.scoring: What to evaluate by ("roc_auc", "f1" and so on)
cv: In cross-validation, how many parts to split the data into (or how to split)
scoring: What to evaluate by ("accuracy", "roc_auc" and so on)
KFold: Splits data into k parts for cross-validation
StratifiedKFold: Splits data into k parts, keeping the answers' proportions the same
GroupKFold: Splits so the same group (such as the same cow) is not in both training and test
n_splits: How many parts to split into
shuffle: Mixes the order of the data before splitting
GridSearchCV: Tries every combination of parameters and picks the best by cross-validation
predict: Predicts answers with the trained model
predict_proba: Predicts the probability of each class
decision_function: The distance from the decision boundary (a score, not a probability)
score: Performance on the test data (accuracy for classification, R² for regression)
transform: Applies a learned transformation (standardization, dimensionality reduction and so on)
fit_predict: Learns and predicts at once (clustering and so on)
linear_model: Linear models (linear regression, logistic regression, Ridge, Lasso)
Ridge: Linear regression with L2 regularization (keeps coefficients small)
Lasso: Linear regression with L1 regularization (sets unneeded coefficients to 0)
alpha: The strength of regularization. Larger makes the coefficients smaller
C: The inverse of the regularization strength. Smaller means stronger regularization
max_iter: The maximum number of learning iterations
solver: The calculation method used for learning
l1_ratio: The share of L1 regularization (0 is L2, 1 is L1)
KNeighborsClassifier: k-nearest-neighbor classification. A majority vote of the k nearest points
n_neighbors: How many nearby points to look at (k)
kernel: The SVM kernel ("rbf", "linear" and so on)
max_depth: The tree's maximum depth (deeper splits more finely but overfits more easily)
min_samples_split: The minimum number of data points needed to split a branch
plot_tree: Draws a decision tree as a figure
filled: Colors the boxes in the decision tree figure
rounded: Rounds the corners of the boxes in the decision tree figure
RandomForestClassifier: Random forest (a majority vote of many decision trees)
GradientBoostingClassifier: Gradient boosting (each tree fixes the previous trees' mistakes)
learning_rate: How much one tree counts (smaller learns more slowly)
preprocessing: Preprocessing (standardization, normalization, discretization and so on)
KBinsDiscretizer: Divides numbers into ranges and makes them categories (discretization)
encode: How the ranges are expressed ("onehot-dense" and so on)
strategy: How the ranges are decided ("uniform" is evenly spaced, "quantile" is equal counts)
pipeline: Chains preprocessing and a model into one
make_pipeline: Chains preprocessing and a model into one
PCA: Principal component analysis. Finds the axes with the most spread and reduces dimensions
n_components: The number of components (axes) to keep
components_: The directions of the principal components (axes)
explained_variance_ratio_: The explained variance ratio (the share of spread each axis explains)
NMF: Non-negative matrix factorization (splits into components with no minus values)
manifold: Manifold learning (t-SNE and other dimensionality reduction for viewing)
TSNE: t-SNE. Lays points out in 2-D so near things stay near and far things far
KMeans: k-means. Splits data into k groups
n_init: How many times to start over with different initial values
AgglomerativeClustering: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering (joins the closest things first)
DBSCAN: Clustering by density. You do not need to set the number of groups
min_samples: In DBSCAN, the number of nearby points needed to be a core point
RFECV: Removes features one at a time with cross-validation and picks the best set
SelectFromModel: Chooses features by a model's importances
step: The number of features removed at a time
classification_report: A table of precision, recall, F1 and so on for each class
confusion_matrix: The confusion matrix (counts of each true answer and prediction pair)
roc_curve: The ROC curve (false positive rate and true positive rate)
roc_auc_score: The area under the ROC curve (AUC)
f1_score: The F1 score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall)
log_loss: Log loss (how bad probability predictions are)
adjusted_rand_score: How well clustering matches the correct answer (ARI)
normalized_mutual_info_score: How well clustering matches the correct answer (normalized mutual information)
scipy: A library for scientific computing (statistics, optimization, clustering and so on)
linkage: The hierarchical clustering calculation (the order of joining)
dendrogram: The tree figure of hierarchical clustering (dendrogram)
truncate_mode: How to leave out the lower part of a dendrogram
method: How to join ("ward" and so on)
numpy: A library for fast calculations on arrays of numbers (vectors and matrices)
np: Uses NumPy under the short name np (import numpy as np)
shape: An array's shape (the number of elements in each direction). (rows, columns)
size: The total number of an array's elements
std: The standard deviation. ddof=1 divides by n−1 (unbiased)
default_rng: Makes a random number generator. With a seed, you get the same random numbers every time
normal: Random numbers from a normal distribution. normal(mean, standard deviation, count)
uniform: Random numbers from a uniform distribution (every value about equally likely)
ravel: Lines up a multi-dimensional array in one row
tolist: Turns it into a Python list
sin: Sine. Element by element for arrays
log: Natural logarithm (element by element for arrays)
pandas: A library for handling table data (like Excel)
pd: Uses pandas under the short name pd (import pandas as pd)
Series: One column of pandas data (a named 1-D array)
sort_values: Sorts by value. ascending=False sorts largest first
crosstab: A table counting each combination of two columns (a cross-tabulation)
get_dummies: Splits a category column into columns of 0 and 1 (one-hot)
cut: Divides numbers into ranges and makes them categories
bins: The number of a histogram's bins
seaborn: A library for statistical graphs, built on matplotlib
sns: Uses seaborn under the short name sns
pairplot: Lines up scatter plots of every pair of columns
hue: The column used to color by
import: Loads a module (another file or library). You can give it a short name with as, as in import numpy as np
from: Loads only part of a module. from datetime import date
as: Gives another name to something imported, or something opened with with
def: Makes a function. After def name(arguments):, write the body indented
return: Returns the function's answer and ends the function
if: Runs only when the condition is true
for: Takes the contents of a container one at a time and repeats
in: In for, "one at a time from..."; in a condition, "whether it is in..."
set: Makes a set (a container with no duplicates)
int: An integer. int("3") turns a string into an integer
round: Rounds (to the nearest even number at .5). round(x, 1) gives 1 decimal place
sorted: Returns a new sorted list. key= sets what to sort by, reverse=True sorts largest first
zip: Takes items at the same position from several containers as pairs
keys: The list of a dictionary's keys
pip: The tool for installing Python libraries
